name: Complete Spark collaborative settings, scenes, and evolution
description:
Execution: AFK after the first playable Spark slice.

User story:
As a group of writers, we can collaboratively define a thematic setting, frame scenes, challenge beliefs, and let both characters and the world evolve without losing authorship or decision history.

What to build:
Extend the Spark adapter with collaborative setting creation and campaign procedures: original inspiration notes, genre and facts, title, three setting Beliefs, GM attributes, Factions, Ties, Faces, Agendas, participant ownership, scene Platform, Tilt, and Question, collaboration and conflict phases, scene closing and reflection, belief replacement through Inspiration, character Growth, and setting Evolution. Represent setting entities in the adapter namespace with optional stable references into Weave World when that module is active.

Acceptance criteria:
- A group can create a setting through ordered, resumable contributions with explicit ownership, consent, revision history, and deterministic resolution of incomplete or concurrent edits.
- Setting Beliefs, Factions, Ties, Faces, and Agendas are typed, reference-safe, visible to story expressions, and portable without requiring a bundled setting.
- Scene framing records who supplied Platform, Tilt, and Question, validates the question and end condition, assigns the next responsibilities predictably, and feeds the existing Spark conflict loop.
- Inspiration and belief replacement require explicit participant confirmation, retain old and new belief lineage, grant Growth correctly, and trigger setting Evolution only when its conditions are satisfied.
- Evolution changes setting beliefs, attributes, and faction data through reviewable operations and never silently overwrites Weave World canon or canonical character personality data.
- Editor workflows support collaborative setup, scene framing, belief review, and evolution with equivalent source representations and accessible single-user fallbacks.
- Synthetic campaign fixtures use only original people, places, factions, inspirations, and themes and cover setup, several scenes, belief change, Growth, Evolution, save and restore, RON and JSON, Bevy, and PixiJS.
- Documentation separates the CC0 core procedures from Weave-authored collaboration UX and explains optional Weave World interoperation without importing published Spark settings.

name: Epic: Weave World module
description:
Outcome:
Ship an optional Weave World module for defining a world's rules, name, places, location structure, environment, and climate, including concise shorthand for seeding a fictional world from real geographic references.

Requirements:
- Resolve references such as New Zealand, Hokkaido in Japan, the Maldives, or the temperate forests of British Columbia into deterministic, typed environmental seed variables.
- Cover useful climate and environment concepts such as seasonality, temperature and precipitation ranges, biomes, terrain, water, elevation, daylight, weather tendencies, and hazards while preserving units and uncertainty.
- Let authors rename, override, combine, or invent places and local conditions without losing source lineage.
- Expose the resulting world corpus consistently to Weave syntax, editor inspection and authoring, runtime variables, RON, and JSON.
- Treat geographic presets as environmental reference material by default, not as cultural stereotypes; any cultural or linguistic pack must be explicit, independently sourced, licensed, and reviewed.

Acceptance criteria:
- A writer can create, inspect, edit, compile, and consume a world seeded from a concise reference-place declaration.
- Named places, nested locations, local environments, and authored climate overrides survive source/editor round trips.
- Every corpus field carries source, license, units, resolution, and confidence or approximation metadata where applicable.
- Equivalent RON and JSON exports are usable from minimal Bevy and PixiJS examples.
- Community contributors can add a validated world preset without editing Weave core.

name: Enrich characters from birth date and historical context
description:
Execution: AFK with corpus and sensitivity review.

What to build:
Add deterministic character enrichment from year-only, month-day, or full birth dates. A versioned public data pack supplies dated historical events, seasonal context, commemorations, and other authoring prompts tagged with transparent personality-relevance vectors. The module overlaps those tags with the canonical profile to rank possible affinities, tensions, values, memories, or voice cues for author review.

Acceptance criteria:
- Date precision and calendar are explicit; partial dates never imply unknown year/month/day facts, and leap-day/time-zone behavior is documented.
- Each context record carries date/period, place scope, tags/vector, source, license, version, uncertainty, and sensitivity metadata.
- Relevance ranking is deterministic, explainable, and configurable; the same profile/date/pack versions/seed produce the same candidates.
- Historical context is offered as fictional authoring material, not a causal claim about real people; nothing becomes canon until accepted or explicitly auto-approved by project policy.
- The editor shows why each candidate matched, supports accept/reject/edit, records lineage, and detects stale derivations after source inputs change.
- Accepted context and derived character variables round-trip through source, RON, JSON, Bevy, and PixiJS paths.
- Offline runtime packs use only original or compatibly licensed public data with documented provenance.

Additional temporal-context requirements:
- Accept optional versioned calendar, seasonal, environmental, and celestial fact packs, including compatible projections supplied by Weave World, without making any one pack mandatory.
- Context resolution pins calendar, date precision, place scope, time zone, observation or reference period, source version, and content hash; unavailable precision remains explicitly unknown.
- Distinguish measured or calendrical facts from interpretive authoring cues. Weather, climate, season, solar, lunar, commemorative, and historical data never constitute causal personality evidence.
- A missing place, partial date, disputed source, or coarse observation produces bounded uncertainty or no candidate rather than fabricated precision.
- Coverage reports identify which requested dates and places have compatible data and why a context record was selected, skipped, or downgraded.
- Accepted cues can influence authored memories, affinities, tensions, and voice guidance only through the existing review and lineage policy.

name: Specify the open character profile and synthesis contract
description:
Execution: HITL methodology and schema review.

What to build:
Independently specify the public Character Profile, including stable identity fields, partial or full birth-date precision, canonical HEXACO factors/facets and bands, confidence, derived OCEAN, pluggable alignment views, authored inner-life/voice fields, source lineage, and deterministic synthesis/override rules. Separate normative data from optional display and suggestion layers.

Acceptance criteria:
- The specification defines all 24 HEXACO facets, valid band/value forms, missing-data behavior, confidence, and schema evolution.
- OCEAN derivation is documented, reproducible, labeled lossy/derived, and cannot write back or be counted as independent evidence.
- Alignment and date-context extensions declare authority, rationale, version, and provenance and cannot silently change canonical traits.
- Authored, imported, derived, suggested, reviewed, and overridden values have distinguishable states and deterministic precedence.
- Equivalent canonical RON and JSON fixtures plus invalid fixtures cover the contract.
- The specification, fixtures, and algorithms are written from first principles and are original or compatibly licensed with documented public provenance.

Additional contract requirements:
- Define optional, versioned extension records for character templates and sparse overrides, identity and presentation references, normalized expression and preference data, behavioral signatures, accepted role projections, and relationship edges.
- Specify stable identifiers, namespacing, missing-data behavior, source lineage, locks, stale state, review state, and precedence for every extension without making optional domains mandatory.
- A template and its overlay remain separately inspectable; resolving the effective profile is deterministic, and updating a template cannot silently replace an authored override.
- Presentation, role, relationship, expression, alignment, date-context, and tabletop projections cannot write back into canonical personality evidence.
- The same typed operation and diagnostic shapes are usable by source tooling, editor actions, the CLI, RON, and JSON.
- Public fixtures cover omitted extensions, unknown versions, conflicting overlays, stale lineage, invalid references, and forward-compatible preservation policy.

name: Epic: Weave Character module
description:
Outcome:
Ship an optional Weave Character module that creates coherent, author-controlled character seed data from a structured personality profile, alignment views, birth date or year, and relevant historical or date context, then exposes that data to Weave stories and game engines. Extend that system-neutral profile with an optional, selectable tabletop-ruleset projection delivered through the companion Selectable tabletop rulesets epic.

Requirements:
- Use the 24-facet HEXACO model as the canonical behavioral profile with explicit bands and confidence; provide OCEAN or Big Five as a transparent derived view so overlapping evidence is not double-counted.
- Support versioned narrative alignment systems as explainable projections or authored views, never diagnoses or hidden behavioral authority.
- Combine personality with birth date or year and selected date-in-history context through deterministic, inspectable synthesis rules and explicit authority and override policies.
- Expose identity, traits, inner-life fields, voice guidance, alignment, date context, derivation lineage, and any selected tabletop projection as typed variables in syntax and the editor.
- Keep tabletop attributes, abilities, resources, conditions, equipment, advancement, and campaign state in a versioned adapter namespace distinct from the canonical Character Profile. A character may have no active ruleset or one active primary ruleset.
- Never infer physical, intellectual, social, or supernatural rules statistics silently from personality, alignment, birth data, or historical context. Any cross-domain suggestion must be explainable, provenance-aware, and explicitly accepted by the author.
- Specify every mechanic independently from first principles, using original algorithms and synthetic or compatibly licensed public inputs.

Acceptance criteria:
- A writer can create, inspect, revise, validate, compile, and consume a complete synthetic character from public inputs, with or without a supported tabletop adapter.
- HEXACO remains canonical, OCEAN is labeled as derived, and every alignment, date, or ruleset enrichment shows its source, authority, and rationale.
- Generated suggestions never silently overwrite authored canon and can be accepted, rejected, or overridden in text and editor workflows.
- Activating, deactivating, or switching a ruleset does not mutate canonical character fields or perform undocumented cross-system conversion.
- Equivalent versioned RON and JSON character packs, including optional active-adapter projections, are usable from minimal Bevy and PixiJS examples.
- Public fixtures, corpora, weights, rules artifacts, algorithms, and documentation are original or compatibly licensed and safe for distribution from the MIT project, with separately licensed material clearly bounded and all required notices preserved.

name: Add Dungeonpunk character and play support end to end
description:
